headline: Sovereignty, Skepticism & Guardrails
thesis: As AI vendors pour tools into classrooms, education leaders are asking who controls the stack, what the evidence says, and how to protect students along the way.
summary: Today's thread is control and caution. Inside Higher Ed's Oct. 22 column asks whether tech sovereignty can free campuses from Big Tech, citing Syracuse's AI-agnostic platform that reportedly kept AI costs 85% below alternatives, while a Maryland randomized trial found an AI study assistant marginally reduced final grades and only ~15% of students used it. On the product side, EdTech Magazine reports Google's new Classroom-centered Gemini tools, and THE Journal covers OpenAI retiring Custom GPTs for a plugin model and a report that ~30% of monitored organizations saw Teams IT-impersonation attempts. Brookings and ISTE keep the student-protection and teacher-training agenda in view, and 1EdTech's 16-organization learning-mobility alliance advances shared standards.
footnote: Compiled from 11 curated edtech sources · October 23, 2026 · Caveat: direct site fetches were unavailable in this environment, so items come from web search results; several sources had no strictly same-day news and show recent or evergreen items.
